key_insight: Single-qubit re-uploading circuits can match multi-qubit Fourier expressivity at the same encoding budget, yet phase-locking makes first-order training substantially harder.
engineering_relevance: Trading qubit width for circuit depth can preserve representational power while reducing optimization reliability under a fixed training budget.
method: Compare serial single-qubit circuits with two-qubit controls at matched encoding budgets and model classes.
Prove a serial tangent-direction ceiling of 2E+2, versus generically at least 6E+6 for the two-qubit control.
Evaluate gradient descent, Adam and Levenberg–Marquardt on exact flat-spectrum losses and three real-world series.
evidence_signal: At E=32, serial circuits reached the optimum in 3/53/83 of 100 runs under gradient descent/Adam/Levenberg–Marquardt, versus 99/100/100 for the control; real-series tests also favored the control's convergence.
watch_item: Results concern one-dimensional inputs and specific circuit comparisons; convergence gaps should not be generalized to all quantum models or interpreted as demonstrated hardware advantages.
paper_title: Same Spectrum, Harder First-Order Training: Phase-Locking in Single- versus Multi-Qubit Re-Uploading Circuits
